title: The Lord on the Throne
summary: In the year that king Uzziah died, Nephi sees the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, his train filling the temple. Seraphim stand above it, each with six wings: two covering his face, two covering his feet, and two used to fly.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator sees the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, in the year that king Uzziah died; the Lord's train fills the temple.
The seraphim's position is described as "Above it" without repeating the referent.
Each seraph has six wings: two cover his face, two cover his feet, and two are used to fly.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The throne appears elevated within the temple.
Positioning the seraphim above the throne reasonably interprets the phrase "Above it".
unspecified_visual_details: The Lord's facial features and other physical characteristics are unspecified.
The number of seraphim and their appearance beyond the described wings, faces, and feet are unspecified.
Temple architecture, throne design, colors, and lighting are unspecified.
Nephi's appearance and viewing position are unspecified.

narration.text: I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.
Above it stood the seraphim; each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The task explicitly identifies the first-person narrator as Nephi; the verses do not independently name him.
King Uzziah's death establishes the year, not a separate event to depict.
The Lord's visible depiction is authorized by the narrated sight, limited to the appearance actually described.
Combined narration and dialogue total 48 words.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict king Uzziah's death or place him in the temple.
Do not invent dialogue, additional events, or additional divine appearances.
Do not assign undescribed features to the Lord or seraphim as source-established facts.
Do not assert a specific physical position for Nephi.

explicit_facts.text: One cried to another and spoke of the Lord of Hosts and his glory.
The posts of the door moved at the voice of the one who cried.
The house was filled with smoke.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Smoke can be shown inside the house.

unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearances of the two figures are unspecified.
The house’s design and the smoke’s appearance are unspecified.

title: The Holy Seed
summary: A tenth is foretold to return and be eaten. A comparison to trees describes their remaining substance, and the holy seed is called the substance thereof.

explicit_facts.text: A tenth is foretold to return and be eaten.
The verse compares this to a teil-tree and an oak whose substance remains when they cast their leaves.
The holy seed is called the substance thereof.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the appearance of the tenth and the holy seed are not specified.

narration.text: But yet there shall be a tenth, and they shall return, and shall be eaten, as a teil-tree, and as an oak whose substance is in them when they cast their leaves; so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The trees are a comparison, not a narrated visible event. The return and being eaten are foretold, not shown happening.
